report:
Trouvailles :

Il y a un important épanchement intra-articulaire avec un petit poplité non-rupturé. Il y a des changements inflammatoires des tissus mous au pourtour du genou. 

Il y a une déchirure complète de la partie centrale du ligament croisé antérieur. Il y a une déchirure complète de l’origine du ligament collatéral interne incluant la composante superficielle et la composante méniscofémorale profonde. L’insertion distale du ligament collatéral interne demeure intacte. 

Il y a une contusion osseuse à la partie latérale du genou compatible avec un récent mécanisme de pivot. Il y a une petite fracture sous-chondrale non-déplacée impliquant la partie postérieure du plafond tibial externe.

Chondropathie du compartiment interne et fémoropatellaire, de degré modéré.

Autrement, le ménisque interne, le ménisque externe, le mécanisme des extenseurs, le semi-membraneux, le muscle et le tendon du poplité, le biceps femoris distal, le ligament collatéral externe et la bandelette iliotibiale sont sans particularité. 

Conclusion :

Déchirure complète du ligament croisé antérieur. 

Entorse de grade 3 du ligament collatéral interne tel que détaillé ci-haut. 

Important épanchement intra-articulaire avec kyste poplité.

Diz eklemi içi sıvı miktarı orta derecede artmış. Arka çapraz ve yan bağlar normal. Ön çapraz bağda tam kat ya da tam kata yakın yırtık izleniyor. Lateral femoral kondil ve lateral tibyal plato posteriyor köşesinde kemik kontüzyonu izleniyor. Posterolateral ve posteromedyal köşe yapıları korunmuş. Medyal menisküs ve lateral menisküs normal. Eklem kıkırdakları ve kemikler bunların dışında normal. Medyal patellar sinovyal plika milimetrik çaplı ve eklem aralığına interpoze değil. Patellada laterale hafif psödosubluksasyon izleniyor. Popliteal fossa hafif ödemli.

There is proximal non avulsive disruption of the anterior cruciate ligament, with some anteriorly displaced fragments being best appreciated in the sagittal plane.  
Marrow contusional changes are noted at the central portion of the lateral femoral condyle, also affecting the posteromedial and posterolateral tibial plateaux - the overall pattern being compatible with a pivot shift mechanism of injury.  
There is a significant resultant suprapatellar effusion with associated synovitis.  There are no convincing medial or lateral meniscal tears. A grade 1 proximal MCL injury is noted. There is furthermore a posteromedial meniscocapsular sprain. 
No posterolateral corner injury is identified, nor is there any injury to the anterolateral ligament. 
Normal PCL, lateral collateral ligament, popliteus musculotendinous unit and PTFL, distal iliotibial band and extensor tendons. Well-preserved tricompartmental hyaline articular cartilage surfaces.  
The extent of fluid signal intensity within the deep posterior soft tissues following injury suggests prior posterior capsular disruption.

MRI of left Knee with SG PD FatSat, SG T2W FS, SG T1W, CO T2W FS, AX T2W FS

* The contour of ACL is not in a straight line and increase signal intensity inside, in favor of tear.
* Linear signal intensity in posterior horn of medial meniscus, it extends into the surface, R/O tear.
*  Linear signal intensity in lateral meniscus, without significant extends into the surface, R/O grade 2 intrasubstance signal.
> The contour of MCL is not all in a straight line and increase signal intensity inside, R/O grade 2 injury.
* Bone marrow edema at the distal femur and proximal tibia, more significant at lateral femoral condyle.
* Massive joint effusion with fluid-fluid interface and suprapatellar bursitis with suprapatellar, medial and lateral plicae; hypertrophy of the synovium, indicative of synovitis.
* Subcutaneous edema around knee.
> The contour of PCL and lateral collateral ligament appear to be within normal, no abnormal signal intensity is noted.

Impression:
1. ACL tear.
2. R/O tear of posterior horn of medial meniscus.
3. R/O grade 2 injury of MCL.
4. Bone contusion of  distal femur and proximal tibia.
5. In favor of hemarthrosis and suprapatellar bursitis with plicae.

Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation.

MRI LEFT KNEE  (plain)

Clinical information:
Left knee pain and stiffness. Ultrasound shows a large complex collection at the posterior joint, MRI suggested. 

Technique: 
Multiplanar MR of the knee according to protocol.

Comparison: 
Ultrasound report dated [Date]

Findings: 

Menisci

Lateral meniscus: intact

Medial meniscus: Several tears of the medial meniscus noted. Radial tear close to the posterior root of the medial meniscus and another inferior surfacing horizontal tear is seen at the posterior horn. Radial tear with truncation also seen at the body of meniscus, which is attenuated in size. Most of the medial meniscus is extruded from the jointline, approximately 0.4cm medial to joint line. 

Ligaments

Anterior cruciate ligament: intact

Posterior cruciate ligament: intact 

Medial collateral ligament: Superficial and deep components intact. Thickening of the superificial component of the medial collateral ligament with moderate periligamentous edema is suggestive of moderate sprain. 

Lateral collateral ligament: The iliotibial band, biceps femoris tendon, fibular collateral ligament and popliteus muscle and tendon intact. 

Posterolateral corner structures: Intact

Extensor Mechanism

The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact. The patella is normally positioned within the femoral groove. There is no retinacular disruption.

Fluid

Moderate knee effusion noted with evidence of synovitis. Thinned wall Baker's cyst with thin septations measuring 4.1cm x 3.4cm x 6.1cm (TSxAPxCC) is seen, consistent with a complex Bakers cyst. No fluid fluid level is seen..Small amount of fluid at the posterior knee is probably secondary to previous rupture.

Mild prepatellar bursitis observed. 

Osseous and Articular Structures

Bones: Mild oedema is seen at the anterior aspect of the medial tibial plateau. Moderate degenerative changes with osteophytosis of all three compartments noted. No fracture, stress reaction, or osseous lesion is seen.

Patellofemoral compartment: Full thickness chondral loss and fissures most observable at the patella apex and medial patella facet, associated with subchondral oedema. 

Medial compartment: Minimal chondrosis. 

Lateral compartment: Minimal chondrosis. 

Others:

Hoffas fat pad: clear

Muscles: Severe atrophy and fatty infiltration of the semimembranosus muscle. 

Neurovascular bundle: Normal 


COMMENT

1.	Multiloculated Bakers cyst with prior rupture. No evidence of haemorrhage or active inflammatory changes. 
2.	Several tears of the medial meniscus, including a radial tear of the posterior root, horizontal tear of the posterior horn and truncation of the inner free edge of the body of medial meniscus. Medial meniscal extrusion noted. 
3.	Moderate sprain of the superficial component of the medial collateral ligament. It is intact with no tear. 
4.	Severe patellofemoral chondral loss and fissures with subchondral oedema. Otherwise only minimal chondrosis at the tibiofemoral joint. Osteophytes in all three compartments.
5.	Mild prepatellar bursitis.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Left knee pain 10 months associated with jumping and activity. History of prior injection.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture. Minimal focal increased T2 signal peripheral lateral femoral condyle may reflect resolving low grade osseous contusion. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
No joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Trace Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: Focal partial-thickness cartilage loss along the central weightbearing medial femoral condyle.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Heterogeneity at the median ridge compatible with low grade cartilage loss. No focal high grade cartilage defects.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: Moderate distal quadriceps insertional tendinosis with superimposed edema of the retroquadriceps fat and low-grade interstitial tearing of the posterior lateral insertional fibers. Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 14 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Moderate distal quadriceps insertional tendinosis with low-grade partial-thickness tear of the posterior lateral insertional fibers.
2.	Minimal bone marrow edema peripheral lateral femoral condyle, may reflect resolving low grade osseous contusion. 
3.	Mild patellofemoral and medial tibiofemoral compartment chondrosis.
